Quick summary of what we expect from the Bristol pilot so your team can do a sizing pass:

- Average generation: ~150 output tokens per request (we're using a condensed prompt template)
- Multi-turn sessions: typical dialog length 3–4 turns; some reuse of prefixes; hope caching helps
- Latency requirement: p95 end-to-end generation <= 450 ms for our interactive web UI
- Planned model: finetuned open model (13B-ish family) — tolerate 8-bit/quantized variants if quality holds

Folks — I ran a first-pass capacity calc with the assumptions Emma provided. Short version below; attaching the calc workbook with the line-by-line math.

Assumptions used (conservative):
- Peak concurrency: 120 qps (burst window)
- Avg output tokens/request: 150 tokens
- Tokens/sec requirement at peak = 120 * 150 = 18,000 tokens/sec
- Model family throughput (redwood-optimized runtime): we measured ~6,000 tokens/sec per GPU for the 13B quantized profile at p95 <= 350ms under realistic batching (batch size ~8–12, mixed request lengths). This is dependent on context length and batching distribution.

Sizing options (rounded):
1) Reserved-only (no burst): 18,000 / 6,000 = 3 GPUs. Apply 1.5x safety margin -> 4.5 -> recommend 5 reserved GPUs.
2) Reserved + burst: Reserve 3 GPUs (covers sustained baseline + modest bursts) and configure 2-GPU burst pool (autoscale) to handle short 10–15m spikes. Effective peak capacity = 5 GPUs.
3) Minimal commit + heavy burst: Reserve 2 GPUs + 4-GPU burst pool -> cheaper monthly commit but more reliance on burst availability; higher risk for p95 during noisy bursts.

Notes and caveats:
- These throughput numbers assume use of prefix/KV caching for multi-turn dialogs; without caching, average tokens/sec increases materially (we estimate +25–40% depending on reuse).
- Quantization to Q4_0 profile is assumed; if Bristol insists on FP16 weights, throughput per GPU drops ~25% -> increase GPU count accordingly.
- Batching efficiency matters: we assume typical request arrival patterns that allow batching into sizes of 8–12. Sharp very low-latency single-shot traffic will reduce tokens/sec per GPU.
- p95 latency target is tied to both tokens/sec and batching; 5 GPUs (option 1) gives best headroom to meet p95 <= 450ms consistently with our current profiles.

I attached the workbook: bristol_capacity_calc_v1.xlsx (calc tabs: assumptions, per-gpu-throughput, scenarios).

Couple of practical adjustments from runtime side that change the effective headroom: 

1) Prefix/KV caching: For Bristol's multi-turn pattern (3–4 turns, repeatable system prompts), we can realistically expect 20–30% reduction in repeated token generation if caching is enabled and prompts are structured. That lowers effective tokens/sec requirement from 18k -> ~13.5k if adoption is good.

2) Model fallback: If committed pool is momentarily saturated, route to a compatible quantized model variant (slight quality delta) — this reduces p95 spikes at the cost of marginal quality impact.

3) Batch shaping & request coalescing: We can prioritize latency-sensitive routes with smaller max-batch sizes while letting less sensitive calls take larger batches; this hybrid policy improves p95 without huge throughput loss.

4) GPU profile numbers: the 6k tokens/sec figure is from our internal bench on A100/RTX8000-class instances using token-at-a-time generation tuned in our runtime. If Bristol prefers an external on-prem SKU (e.g., H100), throughput could be 1.2–1.5x (reduce GPUs). We'll call out SKUs in the final proposal.

Recommendation: start with option 2 (reserve 3, burst 2) AND implement prefix caching + hybrid batch shaping. This balances cost vs. p95 risk during the pilot and gives a straightforward path to scale to 5 reserved GPUs if traffic matures.

Karthik

Emma / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick responses. Attached is our recommended plan (summary below) and the workbook for transparency.

Executive summary (pilot-ready commit):
- Recommended reserved commit: 3 GPUs (13B quantized profile)
- Burst pool: 2 GPUs (autoscale for 10–15m spikes)
- Expected effective peak capacity: 5 GPUs -> baseline coverage for 18k tokens/sec peak assuming caching and batch shaping
- Expected p95: ~380 ms with caching and hybrid batching (conservative estimate from our perf tests)
- Safety margin: we model ~20% headroom for unexpected burst variability; commit can be increased to 5 reserved GPUs if Bristol wants a no-burst deterministic SLA for large events.

Operational checklist / next steps:
1) Bristol share sample prompts or a short eval set (requested earlier) -> we will run perf tests on identical prompts and produce an adjusted workbook.
2) Agree on SKU (A100 vs H100) and term length (monthly/annual) — SKUs affect per-GPU throughput numbers.
3) Procurement: if you confirm a 3+2 commit, we'll send a tailored quote and a DocuSign order form.

Attachments: bristol_capacity_calc_v1.xlsx, slo_latency_matrix.pdf

Happy to set a 30-minute call to walk through the workbook and the fallback policies.

Best —
